question: Which function key can be used with Alt to close the current application in Windows applications?
solution:
The correct answer is __**F4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Alt + F4** in Windows applications closes the currently active application or window.
 
• This keyboard shortcut is a universal command in Microsoft Windows operating systems to terminate the application in focus.
 
• It is particularly useful for quickly closing programs without using a mouse or navigating menus.
 
• The **Alt key** modifies the function of the F4 key, enabling this specific operation.
 
• If no applications are active, pressing **Alt + F4** will display the "Shut Down Windows" dialog box.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Function Keys Overview:**

 
 
• The **F1-F12 keys** are called function keys and are designed to perform specific tasks, often in combination with modifier keys like Alt, Ctrl, or Shift.
 
• Each function key has a unique purpose depending on the software or operating system in use.
 
 
 
• **Alt Key:**
 
 
• The **Alt** (short for "Alternate") key is a modifier key on keyboards used to access alternative functions of other keys.
 
• When used with function keys, it activates specific shortcuts, such as Alt + F4 to close applications.
 
 
 
• **Other Common Keyboard Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Ctrl + C:** Copy the selected content.
 
• **Ctrl + V:** Paste the copied content.
 
• **Ctrl + Z:** Undo the last action.
 
• **Alt + Tab:** Switch between open applications.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Keyboard Shortcuts:**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts improve efficiency and productivity by reducing reliance on the mouse.
 
• They are particularly valuable for users who work extensively with software and multitasking environments.
